learning_outcomes.text: Knows and understands the meaning of all concepts discussed within the "Power Electronics" module.
Knows the most important properties and operating principles of basic semiconductor elements.
Has knowledge of the applicability range of power electronic devices.
Can design a simple power electronic circuit.
Can assess the positive and negative effects of power electronic circuits.
Understands the need for continuous monitoring of power electronics development and continuous self-improvement in this area.

syllabus_topics: Areas of application for power electronics
Principle of operation and properties of basic power electronic components: power diodes, SCR thyristors, IGBT transistors, power MOSFET's
Basic power electronic circuits: AC/DC converters (rectifiers), DC/AC (inverters), DC/DC (choppers), AC/AC (power controllers)
Passive elements in power electronics (chokes, transformers, capacitors)
Familiarization with basic tools for designing and modeling power electronic circuits
Execution of a given power electronic circuit design and verification through simulation studies
assessment_rules: A positive final grade requires obtaining a positive grade from each laboratory exercise. The average of laboratory grades obtained in all terms will be calculated. The final grade (OK) is determined based on the following: if average > 4.75 then OK:=5.0, else if average > 4.25 then OK:=4.5, else if average > 3.75 then OK:=4.0, else if average > 3.25 then OK:=3.5, else if average > 3.0 then OK:=3.0, else OK:=2.0. If the student attended at least 80% of the lectures, the instructor has the right to raise the final grade by 0.5 degree. The project task must be completed with a positive grade.
